note: Hand-entered signals about institutional reports, with publication dates. 'date' is the publication date, not the detection date. Labels follow the Risk Radar vocabulary.

items.label: New report
items.title: IMF GFSR October 2026: financial stability risks remain elevated
items.text: Names a possible correction in AI-related asset prices, sharp rises in sovereign yields, non-bank liquidity mismatches and cyber threats.

items.label: Additional independent assessment
items.title: IMF adds a financial-stability view on cyber threats, alongside ENISA and NCTV
items.text: Cyber risk now has four independent institutional assessments in Risk Radar (ENISA, NCTV, IMF, International AI Safety Report).

items.label: Potential cross-sector link
items.title: AI, cyber and finance: three fields describe overlapping exposure
items.text: ENISA and the AI Safety Report document AI-assisted attacks; the IMF names cheaper AI-enabled attack tools as a driver of cyber risk to finance and separately flags AI-linked asset valuations.

items.label: New report
items.title: ECDC weekly threats report, week 42: Ebola, mpox, West Nile, dengue, chikungunya, CCHF, diphtheria
items.text: Weekly epidemic intelligence for the EU/EEA. The weekly report is still published as of week 42.

items.label: New report
items.title: UN Global Risk Report 2026: large-scale war shows the largest rise
items.text: Survey of 1,300 stakeholders in 155 countries; 36% expect large-scale war to have a significant impact within a year.

items.label: Conflicting evidence
items.title: Perceived importance of environmental risks fell while physical indicators worsened
items.text: UN survey: environmental risks slightly declined in perceived importance. WMO (May 2026): 91% chance of a year above 1.5 °C by 2030.

items.label: New risk identified
items.title: EFSA flags four emerging food-safety risks from 2025
items.text: Examples include bongkrekic acid and the illegal use of a substance to make fish look fresh.

items.label: Revised assessment
items.title: Hunger Hotspots: Nigeria and Somalia move into the highest-risk category
items.text: 13 hotspots for June–November 2026; conflict the main driver in 12.

items.label: Revised assessment
items.title: World Bank cuts 2026 global growth forecast to 2.5%
items.text: Weakest growth since COVID; severe energy-disruption scenario 1.3%.

items.label: New report
items.title: SIPRI Yearbook 2026: 12,187 nuclear warheads; China's arsenal grows fastest
items.text: States rely more on nuclear weapons as escalation risks grow.

items.label: Revised assessment
items.title: WMO: 91% chance of at least one year above 1.5 °C in 2026–2030
items.text: 75% chance that the 2026–2030 average exceeds 1.5 °C; 86% chance of a new record year.

items.label: Revised assessment
items.title: FAO/WOAH/WHO keep H5 risk low for the general public
items.text: Low to moderate for people exposed through work or backyard poultry; no human-to-human transmission identified.

items.label: New report
items.title: International AI Safety Report 2026 published
items.text: Over 100 experts; testing could not rule out meaningful AI uplift for biological weapons.

items.label: New report
items.title: WEF Global Risks Report 2026: geoeconomic confrontation tops the 2-year outlook
items.text: Perception survey of over 1,300 experts. Adverse outcomes of AI shows the largest rise over time.
